data.description:
# A stale installed build must fail LOUDLY, not as a plain INDETERMINATE

## Context / Problem
Split out of bug 7cbe, whose ENVIRONMENT repair is complete. This is the durable half: 7cbe cost two
weeks of silent gate degradation, and the reason it went unnoticed is a REPORTING defect in this
repository's code, not the broken install.

WHAT HAPPENED, measured. A stale global build could not parse the dict-shaped `activate` in
`.rebar/criteria_routing.json`, so criteria assembly raised
`CriteriaError: 'activate' must be a list of ids, got dict`. The gate collapsed that into the ordinary
LLM-outage path:

    "llm_ran": false,
    "llm_unavailable": true,
    "llm_error": "step 'review@then/assemble' failed: criteria overlay ...: 'activate' must be a
                  list of ids, got dict"
    "verdict": "INDETERMINATE"

The command exits 2 and still emits a sidecar. The DET tier runs and reports per-criterion pass/fail,
so the output LOOKS substantive. A reader — human or agent — reasonably concludes the TICKET could not
be reviewed. In fact no LLM review happened at all, and the fault was entirely in the installed build.
This is a CONFIGURATION fault wearing an LLM-outage costume.

## Approach
Separate the two failure classes at the point where the verdict's reason is built. An LLM outage
(provider unreachable, rate-limited, credential rejected) and a CONFIG-PARSE fault (the installed
build cannot read this repository's config) are different conditions with different remedies, and
collapsing them is what hid this.

A `CriteriaError` escaping criteria assembly should surface as its own reason — distinct from
`llm_unavailable` — and the message should name the INSTALLED BUILD as the suspect, because that is
where the fault lives. The reader must be pointed at the install, not at the plan.

Consider also a cheap staleness signal: when the running build's commit is far behind the repository's
HEAD, say so at gate time. That is the generalisation — a stale build will find new ways to fail, and
the specific `activate` shape is only the instance we hit.

REJECTED — making the parse failure fatal (exit non-zero with no verdict): the gate is fail-closed by
design and callers depend on receiving a verdict. The fix is to make the reason ACCURATE, not to
change the control flow.

## Scope
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/` — where `llm_unavailable` / `llm_error` are set for a failed assemble
  step; add the distinct config-fault reason.
- possibly `src/rebar/llm/criteria/overlay.py` — so the raised error carries enough context to be
  classified without string-matching.
- `tests/unit/` — the discrimination tests.

## Testing
Inject a `CriteriaError` from criteria assembly (a malformed overlay fixture, or monkeypatching
`effective_criteria` to raise) and assert on the resulting VERDICT PAYLOAD — the observable a reader
actually sees — never on internal names. Pair it with a genuine LLM-outage case in the same test file
so the two are pinned as distinct rather than merely one being tested in isolation. A negative control
matters here: a real outage must STILL report `llm_unavailable`, or the fix has simply relabelled
everything.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] a test injects a `CriteriaError` during criteria assembly and asserts the verdict payload
      reports a CONFIG-FAULT reason distinct from `llm_unavailable`. This criterion fails against the
      current implementation, which reports `llm_unavailable: true` for that input
- [ ] a NEGATIVE CONTROL test asserts a genuine LLM outage still reports `llm_unavailable`, so the
      change discriminates rather than relabelling every failure
- [ ] a test asserts the surfaced message for the config-fault case names the INSTALLED BUILD (or its
      resolved location/version) as the suspect, so a reader is pointed at the install and not at the
      ticket
- [ ] the DET tier's behaviour is unchanged for both cases — a config fault must not suppress the
      deterministic findings that already run
data.title: A stale installed build must fail loudly, not as a plain INDETERMINATE
